body.text: Run started 2026-11-17T20:57:56Z (authoritative status). Task: sequentially pick 2–3 randomly lying charger plugs, actively reorient each with fingers while following demonstrated wrist style, place blades-up in the left goal zone and clear the right. Stage 1 occupies the full first 60 wall-clock minutes; no robot/task training simulation will be built before 21:57:56Z. Method is one neural network trained from scratch with PPO; no target rounds. First priorities are scene analysis, metric reconstruction, mandatory MANO fit and honest validation.

At ~12 min, initial render-and-compare tracks have median IoU ~0.857 for both chargers but show incorrect blade-axis branches and depth drift during rest. Silhouette scores do not establish physical correctness. I am fitting exact table-supported side/up poses with shared table height and using stationary object geometry to estimate camera translation. A background-only homography decomposition was rejected: 34 cm apparent camera translation and normal dot 0.83 contradict the modest motion; retain its failure evidence. No robot training simulation has been built.

body.text: Stage1 reflection: high mask agreement alone hid wrong orientation branches, resting-depth drift, absent thumb opposition, finger intersections, a palm passing through a finite table slab, and a carried object touching the table. Physical support/identity constraints, anatomy-aware MANO fitting in owned copies, full-vertex checks and manual trajectory/video review resolved them without changing validator thresholds. Final reference r0012/version5 has all10checks passing; monocular absolute depth, invisible contact and material properties remain uncertain. These limitations will inform the verification claims and domain randomization. Simulation remains deferred until the full60minutes end at21:57:56Z.

Simulation construction after reconstruction hour and criteria r0014: own copy of public reference controller, MuJoCo3.17 native deterministic CPU evaluator and Warp batched training. Added conservative sampled column barrier, held-object arm-collision checks, true contact-wrench J-transpose torque halt, all four side faces, matching randomized physical table extents and distal/cross-finger self-collisions. Vendor proximal soft covers overlap the palm by4–12mm at the specified open pose; exclude only palm↔finger-link2 designed overlaps. Corrected free hold has~0.04mm contact penetration and no hardware violations. Local64 deployment starts pass harness support/stillness check64/64; underlying sampler uses25% touching, half leaning, full heading/all4faces and uniform2/3objects. Fixed anatomical wrist→palm rotation from reconstructed MANO axes,20mm offset along human finger direction chosen from public hand reach, retained in reference_calibration.json before suite/policy. Investigating geometry-derived three-finger contact paths for feasibility only; final network remains PPO from random weights, no action labels.

Validation caught a simulator bug before freezing: directly changing native MuJoCo mass/COM without mj_setConst made resting plugs bounce and lose contact (19/64 supported-start checks passed). Recomputing native constants fixed64/64 on the same seeds. GPU free-body inverse-weight constants are now recomputed analytically from mass, inertia and COM and will be checked against the CPU; outcome parity is not yet established for contact-rich manipulation. The corrected sampler rejects physically invalid proposals before the episode, preserving free/touch/lean mode draws; all7 sampled leaning starts actually lean and touch another object, unlike4 earlier proposals that stood upright. The palm/object kinematic reference replay is94.7% reachable at10mm/.05rad, with7.84mm maximum open-hand/object overlap; it is shaping geometry, not a physical controller or evidence of feasibility. No criteria thresholds were relaxed.

body.text: Native full-ramp test of the GPU finger-turn candidate failed transfer: opposed relative rotation58.3deg, World59.7deg, passive15.1deg, then release/drop by14.5s. The right-view montage shows thumb/index holding a corner while the body gradually descends and loses contact near14.3s. GPU best had69/71deg,5s retained, so it is NOT evidence of native task success. Diagnosis: brittle contact trajectory, endpoint hand-off loses support, and contact-rich CPU/GPU parity is unresolved. I will optimize from the native acquired state and score final retained goal/contact margins rather than reward historical progress after a drop. Feasibility controllers remain separate from eventual PPO and supply no labels/weights. New native-search allocation: up to30min/2000 rollouts, expect retained active turn in first500; if plateau, change control parameterization rather than assert parity.

Kinematic placement screening exposed an evaluator defect: the arm/table stop inherited from the GPU starter checks only the lower capsule endpoint inside the table XY bounds. A slanted capsule or its radius can hit a table edge while that endpoint lies outside. Hardware ARM.md section7 requires any arm-link/table touch to stop, so I will replace this approximation in my working copy by segment-to-finite-table-AABB distance with capsule radius. No contact-rich policy/task feasibility has passed; earlier results remain recorded. Frozen evaluator_v3 will not be edited; a new physical simulation record and task suite will follow. Existing high-lift CEM results remain diagnostics and will be rechecked under the corrected stop before relying on them.

body.text: The retained native finger turn still loses its two-finger corner grip when the palm begins the upright carry. Force-QP stabilization with absolute velocity made it worse (drop,24.1deg passive); it is unkept. I am testing a different feasibility-only controller: native short-horizon grip MPC,12 bounded hand-target samples over0.4s every0.2s, no changes to actual dynamics/stops, predicting cloned states and executing only selected contract targets. Budget20min for this parameterization, expect retained object during first carry diagnostic; if no improvement after that, use a post-turn regrasp waypoint search. The actor will never call this planner or receive its actions/weights as labels. Criteria3 and full-task proof remain unchanged/unmet.

Acquisition parameterization now canonicalizes +Y by fixed S=Rz90 before both pose generation and style scoring, and selects a heading after grasp bias using public IK+capsule clearance.24-generation/3.686M-step searches ended with57% white and43% black +Y style-gated GPU acquisitions, no hw violations in final populations; native transfers are pending. This is progress in nominal components, not full-task proof. Extend acquisition search by another7.4M steps/15min for the opposite demonstrated wrist family, with exact finite-board clearance in heading selection. Expect nonzero native-safe acquisition candidates within first1M; otherwise diagnose reachable wrist/finger geometry. Feasibility only, no PPO labels.

MPC montage (local native_turn_mpc, right view12–17s) shows body descending between thumb/index then losing grip around15s, before meaningful transport.12 independent small hand samples did not find coordinated pressure. Within the20min MPC budget, add four proposal candidates that close the actually contacting fingers toward the body centre via their public Jacobians (0.05–0.30rad normalized joint displacement), then let native look-ahead select among these and the old samples. These are feasibility planner proposals only; actual actions still obey PD/effort limits, and contacts are logged only from physics. Predict retention through initial upright carry, not full-task success.
